Question: What is your idea of a perfect relationship or a perfect marriage?
Old_Answer: An old, experienced man was traveling on a train. In the same compartment, a couple was also traveling. They were in their early 40s. At every station, small or big, the man got down from the train and got something for the woman - Coffee, fruit, chocolate, cookies, etc. Even though the woman denied eating, the man persuaded her to have them. The older man was observing everything, and then he asked the woman about her relationship with the man at one station when he got down searching for something. "Who is he?" He asked. "He is my husband." She answered. "No, he is not your husband." The older man replied. "Why? How can you say that?" She felt a little bothered. "A husband will never do so much. You are telling a lie." The older man smiled. The woman found some affection in his smile and confessed that he was not her husband but her husband's friend who was in love with her. While telling the truth, she blushed, and the happiness on her face was quite visible. This is a story, and I am sure many of you can relate to the statement that a husband will never do so much. Because, at some point in time, marriages lose their charm. The spouses take each other for granted. Getting attention from your partner seems like a dream. That's why I mentioned once that marriages should come with expiry dates. Suppose it has to expire in the next year, then the spouses will do their best to keep the relationship alive if there is a dependency from any side. They will long for the renewal of the marriage at any cost, and for that, they will try to keep their spouse happy and content. Then, no need to have a boyfriend or girlfriend from outside. What a great idea! No? Think about it. We are so conditioned by society that we cannot think of anything beyond the cultural norms. P.S.- this write up is not to glorify the extra marital affair but it talks about an idea of keeping the relationship/marriage lively for a lifetime. By the way, that older man was no one but Osho.😊 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
Answer_with_writing_sample: A perfect relationship or marriage, in my opinion, is one where both partners continuously nurture a space of mutual respect, understanding, and unwavering support. From my own experiences, I’ve realized that perfection doesn’t lie in the absence of disagreements but in how we handle them. It's about maintaining open lines of communication, where both partners feel safe to express their feelings without the fear of judgment. A perfect marriage should be a partnership where each person celebrates the other’s successes and comforts them during failures. It’s when both individuals can share their dreams and work together to achieve them, regardless of how big or small they may be. Trust plays a vital role; it’s the foundation that allows both partners to feel secure and cherished. I believe that laughter and joy should be interwoven into the fabric of their interactions, helping to lighten heavy moments and bring them closer. Also, a perfect relationship allows for individuality, letting each partner grow and evolve while still being there for each other. It’s about creating shared memories, having adventures, and learning from each other through life’s ups and downs. Ultimately, a perfect relationship is not about being perfect together but about embracing imperfections and finding beauty in the journey. There’s always room for growth, and with commitment and empathy, partners can carve out a beautiful life together. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

It's a continuous journey of learning, adapting, and growing together, and if both partners are willing to invest in it wholeheartedly, then I believe they can create something truly exceptional and lasting.

Question: I am so alone. I am depressed and lonely and have no friends or significant other. What is wrong with me that makes me so lonely in life?
Old_Answer: For the last two days, I have been feeling like you. I was down in the dumps and had no one to share my feelings with. The more I craved someone with whom I could share my pain freely, the more I felt stifled. "I am no one's priority. No one is concerned about my well-being. There is no one to enquire if I have eaten food or slept well." this thought made me sicker. I hardly ate or drank water. I suffered from insomnia, and during office hours, I dozed off. I felt too fragile even to walk. Out of exasperation, I got furious with a little mistake of my child, yelled at him, and ended up with shedding tears. My sister from far away sensed my despairs and called me to know how I was doing. I enthusiastically exaggerated the taste of chicken soup that I had recently cooked for my child. She couldn't guess what I was going through. This is how a depressed person acts. I felt like consulting a psychiatrist this morning because my depression doesn't seem to fade. Most of the time, I am bright, chirpy, and upbeat, but occasionally, I am clutched by low spirits. And life feels static and pointless. However, in the afternoon, I picked up a storybook by Ruskin Bond and started reading it. After reading a few pages, I felt a little stable. And then, I took the chance to analyze my life, past experiences, desires, and needs. "What is the guarantee that someone (if I find one) will keep me happy?" I asked myself. In the last four years, I have worked very hard to regain my mental peace which I can't ruin by giving someone else the remote control of my life. I have seen people who brutally walked out from my life without giving notice. Come on! I can't make the same mistake. I will work on myself. I am already in love with my aloneness and a bit of loneliness - I will convert it into fulfilling solitude. If I have taken responsibility for my life, I will ensure it is more gratifying. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
Answer_with_writing_sample: I understand how overwhelming loneliness can feel, and it’s a struggle many people face at different points in their lives. I remember when I was in a similar situation, feeling like I was in a dark room with no way out. I often asked myself, “What is wrong with me?” I found that the answers were not always about me but rather about my circumstances and perceptions. Loneliness can stem from a lack of genuine connections or fear of vulnerability. For many, the fear of rejection can be paralyzing, leading to missed opportunities for friendship. I realized that it was crucial to shift my mindset; instead of focusing on what I lacked, I started to embrace small steps toward change. I began engaging in activities I loved, which allowed me to meet like-minded individuals, even if it felt daunting at first. Volunteering or joining hobby groups can be a gentle way to step out of isolation. Remember, it’s okay to seek help; talking to a professional can provide clarity and guidance. Sometimes, self-compassion and giving yourself grace during this period can help you see your worth. There’s nothing inherently wrong with you; life’s journey has its ups and downs. By taking small, proactive steps and being open to new experiences, you may find the connections you seek. Stay hopeful; change is possible. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What should I do if I heard people start gossiping about me?
Old_Answer: Recently, I heard something that made me split my sides. A relative told my mother what other relatives said about me. When I divorced my husband, they spread the rumor that I had an affair and would marry that guy after my divorce. Four years have passed since the separation, and I am still single. However, in these four years, my life became more stable; I gained more freedom, happiness, and peace and established myself as an author. The imaginary guy my relatives saw in their dreams didn't meet me yet, and I am sure he wouldn't ever meet me. Because my taste differs from my relatives, I will definitely not like a guy of their choice and imagination. So I laugh. I enjoy their gossip. And have fun with their rumors. Because I prefer to work on my aspirations rather than pay attention to the blabber of others. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
Answer_with_writing_sample: Hearing people gossip about you can be incredibly unsettling and may lead to feelings of anxiety or frustration. I've been there, and I understand how it feels to be the subject of whispers and speculation. The first step is to take a deep breath and remind yourself that gossip often stems from insecurity or boredom in others. It's not a reflection of your worth or character. Instead of reacting impulsively, consider addressing the situation calmly. If you feel comfortable, confront the gossip directly with the individuals involved. A simple, genuine conversation can sometimes clear misunderstandings. However, if that feels too daunting, focus on building your self-esteem and surrounding yourself with supportive friends who uplift you. Reflect on the kind of person you want to be and let that guide your actions. Remember, gossip often fades when it no longer has an audience. Engage in activities that make you feel confident and fulfilled, shifting your focus from others' opinions to your own self-growth. Lastly, don’t let the negativity consume you; rise above it and remind yourself that you are in control of your narrative. When you choose to live authentically, the opinions of others hold less weight. Embrace your uniqueness, and soon enough, the whispers will die down. Thank you for reading. Stay strong! Anshu.
Answer_with_user_profile: Hearing gossip about yourself can be unsettling, but it's important to navigate this situation with grace and self-awareness. In the grand scheme of life, gossip is often fleeting, whereas your integrity and personal values are lasting. Embrace this opportunity to grow and remain true to yourself, knowing that those who matter will see past the rumors and appreciate the real you.
Answer_with_full_information: Gossip can be one of the most disheartening experiences, especially when it feels like the world is weighing in on your personal life. Question: As a woman, what do some men do that creeps you out?
Old_Answer: Years ago, I was travelling on a train. My co-passengers in my compartment were homely people. There was an old man and his wife, two middle-aged men and a bright young man who was a probationary officer in a bank. Since the journey was nearly 36 hours long, we got along well. The old man liked me for my thoughts and wanted to talk to me more and more. The bank officer grew interested when I shared my opinion on a few topics. The bank officer and I were almost of the same age so we became friends. We shared our Facebook account and he picked up some of my stylish pictures and sent me on WhatsApp commenting something funny but decent. I liked him. He had a great sense of humour. We made fun of everyone on the train through messages and giggled. When we reached our destination, we both exchanged our numbers. At this time, I had grown weary of my monotonous married life though it was just a year old. I really needed someone who could make me laugh. I began to talk to him every day during our office hours. Every day he asked me with care if I had my food on time. I was always smiling and shared the secret of this smile with my husband too. However, slowly, that young man started showing me a different aspect of his personality. He sounded cheap in his talks. His jokes turned obscene and the messages seemed ugly which forced me to block him everywhere. “You need to be careful”, said my husband later. Some men are real creeps. Or I can say, they tend to mistake the inclination that a woman has for them. They walk with a mask on their face which doesn't impress me. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
Answer_with_writing_sample: As a woman, there are several behaviors exhibited by some men that can send chills down my spine. One of the most unsettling actions is when a man invades personal space without consent. I remember an incident when I was simply waiting for my coffee at a café, and a man stood way too close, attempting to strike up a conversation. His proximity made me feel trapped, as if I had no escape from his intentions. This feeling of being cornered is something many women experience when faced with such situations, leading to a heightened sense of anxiety. Additionally, unsolicited compliments can often cross the line from flattering to frightening. I recall a time when a stranger approached me, showering me with compliments about my appearance, but the intensity behind his words felt more like an objectification than a kind gesture. It’s as if some men forget that they are speaking to a person with feelings and boundaries. Then there are the men who persistently message or call despite clear disinterest. I once had an acquaintance who continued to text me even after I politely declined his invitations. This relentless pursuit can be incredibly unnerving, making one feel like a target rather than a person. Overall, it's not just the words or actions but the underlying disrespect for autonomy and boundaries that truly creeps me out. As women, we crave respect and understanding, and when those are absent, it can create an uncomfortable and sometimes frightening atmosphere. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
Answer_with_user_profile: As a woman, certain behaviors from men can indeed feel unsettling, crossing the line from harmless to intrusive. One significant aspect is the unsolicited attention in public spaces; being stared at or approached inappropriately can create an environment of discomfort. For instance, catcalling or making overt comments about one's appearance can feel objectifying and disrespectful. Additionally, there’s the phenomenon of “mansplaining,” where a man explains something in a condescending manner, assuming that a woman lacks knowledge or expertise, regardless of her qualifications. This not only undermines confidence but also perpetuates stereotypes. Another creep-worthy behavior is excessive texting or social media messaging from someone who barely knows you; a barrage of messages can feel invasive and overwhelming, especially if they lack context or consideration for personal boundaries. Equally disconcerting is when men seem to disregard personal space; standing too close or invading physical boundaries can create an atmosphere of unease. Lastly, it’s important to note the subtlety of microaggressions—casual remarks that can reinforce stereotypes or imply inferiority, often couched in humor. They may seem innocuous at first glance, yet they can accumulate, leading to a pervasive sense of discomfort in professional and social settings. Overall, it’s the blend of objectification, lack of respect for boundaries, and condescending attitudes that many women find creepy, highlighting the need for awareness and change in behavior to foster a more respectful and understanding society.
Answer_with_full_information: As a woman, there are numerous behaviors exhibited by some men that can be downright creepy. One major aspect is the unsolicited attention that can manifest in various ways, from persistent staring to inappropriate comments. For instance, I’ve experienced moments where complete strangers approach me with a sense of entitlement, as if my personal space and boundaries do not exist. This lack of respect for privacy makes me feel vulnerable and uncomfortable. Another unsettling behavior is when men insist on sharing overly personal details about their lives, often during initial conversations. It creates a sense of obligation to reciprocate, which feels intrusive and forced. Moreover, the tendency to persistently message or call, even after I've expressed disinterest, can be alarming. This relentless pursuit often leads to a feeling of being stalked, as if the man believes he has the right to invade my time and thoughts. On social media, I’ve noticed that men sometimes slide into DMs with bizarre pick-up lines or unsolicited advice about my appearance, as if they assume their words hold any value. Lastly, the tendency for some men to dismiss or belittle my opinions during discussions is disheartening, making me feel as though my voice is not valued. These experiences contribute to a sense of discomfort and unease, reminding me that, unfortunately, not all interactions are respectful. It’s crucial to recognize and address these behaviors, fostering an environment where women feel safe and respected. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Do Indian parents give smartphones to their children at a young age? If so, why?
Old_Answer: I gave a smartphone to my child when he was eight months old. It sounds weird, but I had no choice. He was not good at eating, and I struggled to feed him every day. I have been a working mother and have always been in a rush. All the passersby knew this adamant child as I fed him, making him sit on the wall near the main gate and showing him dogs and cows. I had hired an adult girl as a caretaker who used to feed him in my absence. It was chaos for that girl as well to feed him every time. However, I noticed he could easily take the first few spoons while watching YouTube videos. That eased our task to some extent. So I permanently gave my smartphone to him and bought a new one for myself. He watched videos while having food until the last year. Now, he watches TV or laptop. I have banned the mobile for him. You can blame me for being an irresponsible mother, but I was helpless. He needed some diversion to swallow the morsel; otherwise, he threw it out. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
Answer_with_writing_sample: Yes, many Indian parents do give smartphones to their children at a young age, and the reasons behind this decision can be multifaceted. I remember when my daughter turned seven; the world around us was changing rapidly, and she often expressed her desire to connect with her friends through messaging apps and online games. At first, I hesitated, fearing the negative impacts of excessive screen time. However, I eventually realized that smartphones have become an integral part of modern life. They serve not just as devices for entertainment but also as tools for education and communication. Parents often believe that giving their children smartphones at an early age can enhance their learning experience. There are countless educational apps that can help children grasp concepts more easily. Moreover, in a country as vast as India, where families sometimes live far apart, a smartphone allows kids to stay connected with relatives, fostering relationships that might otherwise fade. However, it’s essential to balance this access with parental guidance. Setting boundaries around screen time and monitoring the content can help mitigate potential risks like exposure to inappropriate material or addiction to screens. As a single mother, I’ve learned that while technology can seem daunting, it also holds immense potential to prepare our children for a tech-savvy future. Thus, the decision often reflects a blend of necessity, societal pressures, and a desire to give our children the tools they need to thrive. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Ultimately, the decision to grant children access to smartphones reflects a blend of convenience, safety, and social connectivity, making it a common practice among Indian families today.

Old_Answer: My father adored me when I was a little girl. He was so fond of me that he wanted to see me as soon as he returned from his clinic. He would scoop me into his arms, planting a tender kiss on my forehead, tousling my hair and gently rubbing his chin against mine. At night, he would cradle me and we’d playfully roll in bed, creating moments filled with laughter. This was the love he showered on me during the childhood. “I love her the most” He proudly declared to everyone, expressing his deep affection for me. I cherish those beautiful moments the most in my life. Yesterday, my mother conveyed over the phone that he no longer wishes to travel to Bangalore. He says his body no longer supports extensive journeys; he is now 76. I feel a profound sadness, thinking how things change in our life. He is sacrificing his fondness for his daughter and grandson due to his weakened body. And I am struggling to accept this reality. I miss my father, his love and his fondness. Question: What do you think is the easy way that leads us to heaven?
Old_Answer: My grandfather (paternal) was a religious man. He went on several pilgrimages. He never touched non-vegetarian food in his life. He never missed any fast for Ekadashi, which is considered the most auspicious fast in the Hindu religion. He spent his morning and evening offering prayers at the temple that he had only constructed. He donated money and lands to the welfare of society. He built a hospital. He was known for his kindness. He died in his late 80s. I am not sure if he went to heaven, as the concept of hell and heaven doesn't sound promising. However, looking at the crowd that came for his last darshan, I believed that he was God's child. No one in the crowd spoke ill about him. Everyone was just eager to touch his feet and see his face for the last time. Even if the concept of hell and heaven exists, I will not value it much as it comes into existence after death. Instead, I would insist on living like my grandfather, whose demise saddened everyone. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

For me, the easy path to heaven lies in embracing kindness and compassion in our daily lives. It's about the small, seemingly insignificant actions that we often overlook but hold immense power. I remember a time when I was struggling to make sense of my life and felt lost in the chaos. During that period, I focused on helping others, whether it was a comforting word to a friend or lending a helping hand to someone in need. This shift in perspective opened my heart and allowed me to experience a sense of fulfillment that I had never known before. The more I engaged in acts of kindness, the lighter my burdens felt, and the more I began to see the beauty in the world around me. I realized that heaven is not just a distant place but a state of being. When we serve others selflessly, we create ripples of positivity that not only uplift those around us but also elevate our own spirits. Additionally, practicing gratitude for the simple joys in life—like a warm cup of tea or a smile from a stranger—can lead us closer to that heavenly state. So, the easy way to heaven, in my opinion, is to cultivate love and kindness within ourselves and extend it to others. By doing so, we not only transform our own lives but also contribute to a more compassionate world. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: How can I love myself? Are there any tips or a book that can help me start?
Old_Answer: For me, my mental peace is the most important thing in life. I can't compromise on it. I had a boyfriend in the college with whom my inner tranquility was often at stake. Later I was in a marriage where I forgot about my wants and needs. I completely lost my mental health and became insomniac. At present, my emotional well-being is my first priority. I can gracefully exit any relationship where my mental health is at risk, no matter how emotionally involved I am with the person. Because I know how it feels after losing it. So, safeguarding my mental peace is the first sign of loving myself. No book or tip can help you to love yourself. You need to identify your preferences, wants and needs, and then you have to protect them. You need to set boundaries and make sure no one crosses them. Currently, ‘selfless love’ is not in my dictionary. I can only love those who reciprocate the same to me. I make sure I don't chase people blindly. I let people know that they can not take me for granted. It hurts me a lot when I am emotionally involved with someone and that someone neglects me. So, in a relationship, I ensure that I am not hurt. I focus on things that I want in my life. I take care of my health and sleep. This is another version of loving myself. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
Answer_with_writing_sample: Loving yourself is a journey that requires patience and understanding. I remember a time in my life when I felt unworthy, constantly comparing myself to others and feeling inadequate. It was only when I started to shift my perspective that I began to embrace who I am. One powerful tip is to practice self-compassion. Treat yourself as you would treat a dear friend; encourage and support yourself during tough times. This simple act can change your inner dialogue from critical to nurturing. Journaling is another effective tool; write down your thoughts, feelings, and achievements, no matter how small. This helps you recognize your value and celebrate your uniqueness. Additionally, I recommend reading "The Gifts of Imperfection" by Brené Brown. Her insights on embracing vulnerability and cultivating self-worth can be transformative. Engaging in activities that bring you joy, whether it's painting, dancing, or hiking, allows you to reconnect with your passions and rediscover what makes you, you. Surrounding yourself with positive influences who uplift you instead of bringing you down is crucial for cultivating a loving environment. Remember, self-love is not a destination but a continuous practice. Don't hesitate to seek support from friends or professionals if needed. Ultimately, it's about acknowledging your flaws and strengths and understanding that everyone is a work in progress. Embrace the journey, and with time and effort, you’ll find that loving yourself becomes easier. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What should a 21-year-old girl do if she hates household chores?
Old_Answer: She should focus on her career. She should be financially settled to hire a cook and domestic help. Then only she can escape household chores. Otherwise, she has no choice. Though it applies to both genders, it is more applicable to women in our patriarchal society. She is not supposed to sit idle and dictate. A husband is accepted to sit and dictate, but not a wife. Reality! If a woman neither earns money nor does household chores, she is considered useless. And there is nothing wrong with that. To survive, one has to accomplish a few skills. I always had a cook and domestic help to clean the house, but during the COVID, when I was jobless and could not hire a cook, I realized how much cooking skills matter. I learned it in a year. However, my family still considers me dumb when it comes to managing households. Still, I would say — if you are not willing to do household chores, there is nothing wrong with that. It's just a matter of interest. You can utilize your energy and time to do something else and always hire domestic help for your work. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
Answer_with_writing_sample: At 21, hating household chores is quite common, and you’re definitely not alone. I remember when I was in my early twenties, feeling overwhelmed by the mundane tasks that seemed to pile up endlessly. The key is to find a balance between responsibilities and your personal preferences. First, try to simplify your chores. Break them down into smaller, manageable tasks that you can tackle one at a time. For instance, instead of viewing cleaning the entire house as a monumental task, focus on one room or even one area each day. This way, it becomes less daunting, and you won't feel like you're sacrificing your entire day. Moreover, infuse some fun into these chores. Play your favorite music or listen to a podcast while you clean. This can transform the experience from a dreaded obligation to a moment of enjoyment. Additionally, consider involving others. If you live with family or friends, turn chores into a group activity. It not only lightens your load but also makes the task seem more social and less like a chore. Finally, remember that chores are a part of life, but they don’t have to define your day. Embrace your love for other activities and allocate time for them as rewards for completing your tasks. This creates a positive reinforcement loop and can help you navigate the mundane with a better mindset. Thank you for reading, and remember, it's all about finding that balance! Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: How do you judge yourself?
Old_Answer: I look at myself in the mirror and exclaim, “Oh, I am so young, so beautiful, yet to grow and yet to see the world.” When I go out and feel tempted to eat samosa, noodles, or any other junk food, I remind myself of my age, “Shame on you! How can you think of junk food? Look at your age; your skin is getting dull.” And this certainly helps me avoid junk food. Lol! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
Answer_with_writing_sample: Judging oneself can be a complex and often painful process. For many years, I found myself caught in a web of self-criticism and doubt. I would constantly compare my life to others, measuring my worth against their accomplishments. It was only when I started to reflect deeply on my experiences that I realized the importance of self-acceptance. I began to ask myself questions: What have I learned from my struggles? How have I grown as a person? Each answer brought me closer to understanding that my journey is unique and filled with important lessons, even in adversity. In my darkest moments, I learned that self-judgment should not stem from societal standards or the opinions of others but rather from a place of compassion. Instead of focusing on my failures, I started to celebrate my resilience, recognizing the strength it took to overcome challenges. I also learned the power of self-compassion, allowing myself to acknowledge my flaws without harsh judgment. This shift in thinking helped me develop a more positive and realistic self-image. Ultimately, I judge myself based on my growth, my ability to adapt, and the kindness I show to both myself and others. Life is a continuous journey of learning, and with each passing day, I strive to become a better version of myself, appreciating both my strengths and weaknesses. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
